archives: Confirmed MALICIOUS by queue; their verdicts were not re-evaluated or inherited.
scope: Exactly the 75 listed stranded members, at their actual extracted filesystem paths. Debian data/ in queue paths is an archive-layer label; extraction places usr/ directly below the extraction root.
judgment_context: Kali/Empire, DAVTest and SecLists provenance supports legitimate security-testing use. No engagement authorization, installed permissions, live controller configuration or execution telemetry was supplied. The judgments concern operational attack payloads found as files, not an assertion that any payload executed or that every user of these tools has malicious intent. Every verdict uses the member bytes and the identified execution path; scores and names were not treated as proof.
methods: Static source/control-flow review; no sample executed
atomscan --no-update --follow=none --mode slow -f json on every listed member, before and after edits
cleave facts on every member, plus reconstructed PE payloads to expose decoded strings and structured facts
Base64, GZip and Deflate reconstruction of embedded PEs; dnfile/dncil managed IL decoding and rizin native disassembly
ZIP directory/local-header review and a bounded 64-byte ZIP-bomb decode without full extraction
changes: Correct WASAPI capture description to include audio loopback

Move message-window constant and SetParent references from clipboard monitoring to window control; remove ambiguous standalone IntPtr(-3) alternative and make the neutral reference combination notable
Move generic Windows event-log query atoms out of passkey authentication; retain WebAuthn composite only with its channel evidence
Move PowerShell resolver API reference out of DNS-label construction and update both consumers; remove inherited C2 technique mapping from neutral resolver reference
Add notable raw-socket receive-all/header configuration and structured firewall policy/rule object construction calls
coverage_exception: The ten seven-byte traversal payloads each justify one hostile defacement trait and one suspicious built-in traversal finding. A second hostile execution or destruction claim was not invented: they contain no executable PHP and rely on an unsafe extractor. All remaining members already have at least two supported hostile findings.

members.marker_note: WireTap: records keys, audio and images; fix traits
members.behavior: Base64/GZip is decoded into a managed PE, Assembly.Load loads it, and WireT4p.Program.Main dispatches operator commands. IL paths record microphone and speaker audio to WAV, save screen/webcam JPEGs, hook keys, and monitor clipboard text. ListenForPasswords recognizes credential-related speech before a two-minute recording.
members.execution_chain: Invoke-WireTap -> Assembly.Load -> Program.Main -> Audio/Keyboard/Display

members.marker_note: SharpChromium: exports browser passwords and session cookies
members.behavior: The wrapper loads a GZip/Base64 assembly, enumerates Chrome/Edge profile paths, and dispatches GetSavedLogins/GetCookies/GetHistory. Managed IL copies/queries SQLite logins, calls DecryptBlob, and builds plaintext password records. The wrapper formats passwords and serializes cookies.
members.execution_chain: Get-SharpChromium -> DecompressAsm -> ChromiumCredentialManager -> GetSavedLogins/GetCookies

members.marker_note: NetRipper: injects hooks to capture credential traffic
members.behavior: Inject-NetRipper opens selected process handles, patches the embedded DLL configuration with credential search terms and capture paths, allocates remote RWX memory, writes the image, and starts its ReflectiveLoader. The native image contains network read/write hooks and file logging; capture includes plaintext before/after encryption.
members.execution_chain: Inject-NetRipper -> OpenProcess -> VirtualAllocEx -> WriteProcessMemory -> remote ReflectiveLoader

members.marker_note: SharpLoginPrompt: harvests and prints prompted passwords
members.behavior: A Base64 PE is loaded and its Main method invoked. IL calls CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials and CredUnPackAuthenticationBuffer, then prints Username, Password and Domain. ValidateCredentials controls reprompting. This exposes the secret to the caller rather than returning only an authentication result.
members.execution_chain: Assembly.Load -> SharpLoginPrompt.Program.Main -> credential dialog -> password output

members.marker_note: Get-Keystrokes: polls and records keys with window titles
members.behavior: The code defines user32 imports, polls GetAsyncKeyState in a loop, interprets modifier/special keys, translates keys, and emits recorded keystrokes with foreground-window attribution.
members.execution_chain: GetAsyncKeyState loop -> key translation -> foreground title and captured output

members.marker_note: ChromeDump: decrypts and stages saved browser passwords
members.behavior: The script embeds SQLite dependency assemblies, opens Chromium profile databases, selects login records, decrypts password_value with ProtectedData.Unprotect, and emits/writes plaintext credentials. The embedded DLLs are dependencies of this credential acquisition path; their presence alone was not used to convict.
members.execution_chain: SQLite query -> password_value -> DPAPI Unprotect -> credential output/file

members.marker_note: CredentialPhisher: spoofs native prompts to collect passwords
members.behavior: The script loads its helper assembly, constructs application/toast/native credential UI, optionally hides process windows, unpacks returned authentication buffers, and exports password-bearing records. Credential validation can force repeated prompts.
members.execution_chain: Invoke-Prompt -> CredUIPromptForWindowsCredentials -> CredUnPackAuthenticationBuffer -> output

members.marker_note: Inveigh: poisons names and captures NTLM responses
members.behavior: Separate runspaces implement LLMNR/mDNS/NBNS spoofing and HTTP/SMB listeners. NTLM challenge-response processing extracts NTLMv2 material into capture queues/files. This is authentication interception, not an ordinary resolver or HTTP server.
members.execution_chain: spoofers/listeners -> NTLM challenge -> HTTP/SMB response parsing -> NTLMv2_list

members.marker_note: USB ETW keylogger: records USB keystrokes through ETW
members.behavior: Base64/Deflate reconstructs a managed ETW library. IL StartCapture enables USB providers and registers EventCallback; callbacks filter USB transfer events, parse keys, and enqueue them. PowerShell starts capture and drains keysPressed with foreground-window/time attribution.
members.execution_chain: Deflate -> Assembly.Load -> startkeyLog -> USB ETW callbacks -> keysPressed.Dequeue

members.marker_note: FoxDump: decrypts and exports Firefox saved logins
members.behavior: The source resolves NSS decryption functions against Firefox profiles, decodes encrypted login fields, invokes PK11SDR_Decrypt through native delegates, and outputs/stages plaintext username/password records.
members.execution_chain: Firefox profile login records -> NSS decrypt -> plaintext credential output/file

members.marker_note: Mimikatz server copy: reflectively dumps passwords and clears PE magic
members.behavior: The script decodes x86/x64 native PEs, chooses architecture, erases the decoded MZ bytes, maps sections/relocations/imports, and invokes the exported password tool with sekurlsa::logonpasswords by default. Native export disassembly parses command arguments and enters its command dispatcher; process-memory reads support the credential path.
members.execution_chain: Main -> Base64 PE -> reflective loader -> powershell_reflective_mimikatz -> sekurlsa

members.marker_note: DCSync: requests AD replication secrets and parses hashes
members.behavior: This is an executable reflective Mimikatz wrapper. It loads an architecture-specific PE and invokes lsadump::dcsync for selected/enumerated users, then parses returned NTLM material. Native InvokeWide jumps into the command dispatcher. Requires domain replication rights; it is not a standalone rights bypass.
members.execution_chain: reflective PE load -> InvokeWide -> lsadump::dcsync -> NTLM result parsing

members.marker_note: SharpSecDump: recovers SAM hashes and LSA secrets
members.behavior: The GZip/Base64 PE is loaded and its entry method invoked with operator arguments. IL dispatches work per target, retrieves/parses registry hives, decrypts SAM hashes and LSA/cached-domain secrets, and displays recovered records.
members.execution_chain: Assembly.Load -> RegQueryValueDemo.Main -> hive retrieval -> SAM/ParseLsa -> report

members.marker_note: CredStore dumper: enumerates and prints stored password blobs
members.behavior: Embedded C# declares Credential Manager enumeration/read APIs. Enum-Creds calls CredEnum; CredManMain formats each returned CredentialBlob under a Password field with username/target details. This is direct secret export.
members.execution_chain: CredEnumerateW -> Enum-Creds -> CredManMain -> CredentialBlob output

members.marker_note: CredentialInjection: clones Winlogon and injects a logon helper
members.behavior: The script obtains a primary SYSTEM token, creates a suspended Winlogon clone, reflectively injects a native DLL, and exchanges credentials through a named pipe. The DLL export reads pipe data, calls LsaLogonUser, and impersonates the returned logon token.
members.execution_chain: SYSTEM token -> suspended Winlogon -> DLL injection -> named pipe -> LsaLogonUser

members.marker_note: PowerDump: steals a privileged token and decrypts SAM hashes
members.behavior: The privilege helper duplicates an LSASS token and assigns it to the current thread. Registry routines recover boot/SAM key material and decrypt LM/NT hash records with the applicable RC4/DES/AES paths before output.
members.execution_chain: ElevatePrivs -> LSASS token -> SAM/boot-key reads -> hash decryption -> DumpHashes

members.marker_note: SessionGopher: extracts saved remote-access session secrets
members.behavior: The script enumerates local/remote user/session configuration, retrieves remote files through WMI/registry helpers, processes PuTTY/WinSCP/FileZilla/RDP artifacts, decodes FileZilla passwords and reverses WinSCP stored password protection.
members.execution_chain: session enumeration -> config reads -> ProcessFileZillaFile/DecryptWinSCPPassword -> records

members.marker_note: NTLMExtract: impersonates SYSTEM to recover local hashes
members.behavior: Invoke-AsSystem opens a privileged process, duplicates/impersonates its token, and Get-NTLMLocalPasswordHashes reads SAM/boot-key data, derives keys, decrypts hash records and formats the results.
members.execution_chain: Invoke-AsSystem -> privileged token -> Get-NTLMLocalPasswordHashes -> decrypted hashes

members.marker_note: DomainPasswordSpray: sprays passwords across domain accounts
members.behavior: The source collects domain users and lockout policy/observation windows, iterates candidate credentials, and uses DirectoryEntry authentication attempts across many accounts. Timers and lockout checks manage the attack rate.
members.execution_chain: Get-DomainUserList -> observation/lockout policy -> Invoke-SpraySinglePassword -> LDAP auth

members.marker_note: TokenManipulation: steals tokens and launches impersonated children
members.behavior: The script enumerates process/thread tokens, opens and duplicates selected identities, impersonates them, and can create a child with a stolen token. Privilege enabling and desktop ACL manipulation support those execution paths.
members.execution_chain: Get-UniqueTokens -> DuplicateToken -> impersonation/Create-ProcessWithToken

members.marker_note: BypassUAC: plants a hijack DLL and elevated command launcher
members.behavior: The code patches embedded hijack/helper DLLs, writes a command batch launcher, injects a helper into a process, and abuses an auto-elevated DLL search path. Native TPGenProc ultimately reaches CreateProcessA; the batch launcher removes itself.
members.execution_chain: Write-HijackDll -> helper injection -> trusted DLL hijack -> command batch -> self-delete

members.marker_note: SweetPotato: abuses service impersonation for elevated execution
members.behavior: Base64 loads a managed exploit. IL selects COM/WinRM/print/EFS coercion mechanisms, negotiates local authentication, acquires an impersonation token, and starts a supplied program with elevated authority. Requires the relevant service/impersonation prerequisites.
members.execution_chain: Program.Main -> PotatoAPI trigger/listeners -> authenticated token -> process creation

members.marker_note: MS16-032 exploit: races leaked handles for a SYSTEM shell
members.behavior: Get-ThreadHandle uses CreateProcessWithLogonW to leak handles; token routines impersonate the leaked privileged context and race suspended process/thread operations to launch the requested SYSTEM command.
members.execution_chain: Get-ThreadHandle -> leaked handle -> duplicated SYSTEM token -> suspended logon race

members.marker_note: PowerUp: abuses services and recovers stored secrets
members.behavior: The library includes auditing as well as operational abuse: it reconfigures service commands, patches/writes executable service or DLL payloads, builds user-add MSI payloads, and decrypts SiteList/GPP secrets. Its exploitation and password-export implementations tip the verdict beyond a read-only audit library.
members.execution_chain: Invoke-ServiceAbuse/Write-ServiceBinary/Write-HijackDll and SiteList/GPP decryption

members.marker_note: EventVwr bypass: hijacks auto-elevation and removes command overrides
members.behavior: The function writes an attacker command to a registry payload value, overrides the current-user mscfile open command, launches Event Viewer, then removes payload/override properties. The encoded command in documentation is an example, not a configured default command.
members.execution_chain: registry payload -> mscfile shell open override -> eventvwr.exe -> cleanup

members.marker_note: PrintNightmare: loads a printer-driver DLL to gain admin execution
members.behavior: Driver enumeration supplies a legitimate driver path while pConfigFile/pDataFile are replaced with the provided DLL. AddPrinterDriverEx uses copy/installation flags to load it. An embedded default DLL is prepared with user/password values to create a local administrator.
members.execution_chain: get_nightmare_dll -> DRIVER_INFO_2 config/data replacement -> AddPrinterDriverEx

members.marker_note: PrintDemon: writes a System32 DLL and installs a Run launcher
members.behavior: The exploit creates a raw printer port pointing at System32 ualapi.dll, sends decoded native DLL bytes through WritePrinter, and installs a hidden encoded PowerShell Run-key launcher. Native UalStart queues a thread-pool callback.
members.execution_chain: raw printer port -> WritePrinter DLL -> UalStart callback; registry Run encoded launcher

members.marker_note: Get-System: impersonates SYSTEM via tokens or a named pipe
members.behavior: Two paths either arrange a SYSTEM service connection to a named pipe and impersonate its client, or enumerate SYSTEM-owned processes, duplicate a token, and assign it to the thread. This is explicit higher-authority execution context acquisition.
members.execution_chain: SYSTEM service pipe -> ImpersonateNamedPipeClient; or SYSTEM process token -> SetThreadToken

members.marker_note: SDCLT bypass: uses an elevated command association to run payloads
members.behavior: The source creates an IsolatedCommand override under the current-user executable association, starts sdclt with /kickoffelev, and removes the payload and override afterward.
members.execution_chain: exefile runas IsolatedCommand -> sdclt /kickoffelev -> command execution -> cleanup

members.marker_note: FodHelper bypass: hijacks DelegateExecute for elevated execution
members.behavior: The source writes ms-settings shell open command and an empty DelegateExecute value, launches hidden FodHelper, and deletes the installed command properties after a delay.
members.execution_chain: ms-settings command/DelegateExecute -> fodhelper.exe -> payload -> cleanup

members.marker_note: EnvBypass: hijacks windir for SilentCleanup elevation
members.behavior: The source installs a windir environment-registry value containing a hidden PowerShell command and runs the elevated SilentCleanup task through schtasks. Cleanup removes both the hijack and payload value.
members.execution_chain: windir registry override -> SilentCleanup scheduled task -> PowerShell -> cleanup

members.marker_note: GPP password recovery: sweeps SYSVOL and decrypts exposed passwords
members.behavior: The source searches domain SYSVOL preference XMLs, extracts cpassword and related account fields, decodes Base64 and decrypts with the published fixed AES key, returning plaintext credentials.
members.execution_chain: SYSVOL preference XML search -> cpassword -> fixed-key AES -> password records

members.marker_note: Tater: poisons NBNS and reflects NTLM for service execution
members.behavior: The script combines guessed NBNS responses, a local HTTP authentication endpoint, authentication triggers, and SMB NTLM reflection to create/start a local service command. UDP exhaustion and trigger helpers support this exploit chain.
members.execution_chain: NBNS spoof -> local auth trigger -> NTLM reflection -> SMB service command

members.marker_note: UAC token bypass: duplicates elevated tokens to bypass UAC
members.behavior: The code locates or creates a high-integrity process, duplicates its token, changes integrity settings, impersonates the modified token and invokes CreateProcessWithLogonW for the requested payload.
members.execution_chain: high-integrity process -> duplicate token -> integrity change -> impersonation -> child

members.marker_note: MS16-135 exploit: corrupts Win32k objects to replace a process token
members.behavior: Accelerator/window operations groom kernel objects and trigger bitmap pointer corruption. Manager/worker bitmap read/write primitives locate SYSTEM and current EPROCESS records, read SYSTEM Token, and overwrite the current process token.
members.execution_chain: bitmap corruption -> arbitrary kernel read/write -> SYSTEM EPROCESS token -> current token overwrite

members.marker_note: SiteList recovery: decrypts McAfee stored passwords into output
members.behavior: The function searches for or accepts SiteList.xml, reads password fields, reverses Base64/XOR and static-key 3DES protection, then returns plaintext account/server/password records.
members.execution_chain: SiteList XML -> Base64 -> fixed XOR -> static-key 3DES -> Decrypted output

members.marker_note: PowerBreach: callback backdoors; add socket/firewall traits
members.behavior: Invoke-CallbackIEX downloads a Base64 script by HTTP/HTTPS/BITS, decodes it and invokes IEX. TCP-line, DNS-answer, Security-event and raw-packet trigger loops can invoke this callback; another path polls. Add-PSFirewallRules creates enabled allow rules. Get-WinEvent is generic event access, not WebAuthn; DNS resolution is not label construction.
members.execution_chain: network/event trigger -> callback -> download -> Base64/UTF8 -> IEX

members.marker_note: RID hijacker: rewrites SAM identity RID after token theft
members.behavior: The function obtains privileged access through LSASS token duplication, reads the SAM account F record, replaces RID bytes, writes F back, and can change account password/state. Success depends on SAM access and privileged context.
members.execution_chain: LSASS token -> SAM user F value -> RID byte replacement -> registry write

members.marker_note: Reflective VNC: loads remote-control code and erases PE signatures
members.behavior: The source selects embedded architecture-specific VNC native code, constructs VNC connection/password arguments, erases decoded PE magic, reflectively maps the image and invokes it. This is an in-memory control payload rather than a normal VNC installation.
members.execution_chain: VNC args -> Base64 PE -> magic erasure -> reflective native entry

members.marker_note: Metasploit loader: executes downloaded code in a hidden interpreter
members.behavior: A WebClient cradle disables certificate validation, configures proxy credentials, downloads an operator URL and passes its response to Invoke-Expression. The wrapper launches the cradle through a hidden PowerShell process.
members.execution_chain: URL -> TLS-bypassing DownloadString -> IEX inside hidden PowerShell

members.marker_note: SpoolSample: coerces printer RPC authentication to a capture host
members.behavior: The wrapper loads its embedded assembly and calls Main. IL combines TARGET/CAPTURESERVER into UNC arguments and invokes an embedded RPRN native helper export. The payload initiates printer RPC notification/coercion toward the capture endpoint.
members.execution_chain: Assembly.Load -> SpoolSample.Main -> UNC target/capture arguments -> RPRN DoStuff

members.marker_note: Jenkins exploit: posts Groovy command execution and reads results
members.behavior: The source contacts /script, URL-encodes supplied command arguments into a Groovy ProcessBuilder expression, POSTs the script to Jenkins, and extracts execution results from the response. Requires an accessible/misconfigured script console.
members.execution_chain: /script GET -> Groovy ProcessBuilder POST -> request body write -> response result parse

members.marker_note: JBoss exploit: deploys a remote WAR and triggers its JSP
members.behavior: The script sends a HEAD invocation to JMX HtmlAdaptor/MainDeployer with an operator-supplied WAR URL, waits for deployment, then requests the resulting JSP. It can disable HTTPS certificate validation.
members.execution_chain: JMX MainDeployer URL -> HEAD deployment request -> delayed JSP GET

members.marker_note: Inveigh relay: relays captured NTLM into remote service execution
members.behavior: HTTP/proxy authentication handlers capture NTLM response data; the relay state machine forwards authentication into SMB and issues SCM CreateServiceW/StartServiceW commands carrying the configured operator command.
members.execution_chain: HTTP NTLM capture -> SMB relay -> service create/start -> command

members.marker_note: PsExec module: creates and removes a remote command service
members.behavior: The function opens the remote Service Control Manager, creates a service whose command is the supplied payload, starts it and removes the ephemeral service. This implements lateral command execution, not only service inventory.
members.execution_chain: OpenSCManager -> CreateServiceA(Command) -> StartServiceA -> DeleteService

members.marker_note: SMBExec: authenticates over SMB and runs a command service
members.behavior: The script builds SMB/NTLM and DCE/RPC packets, authenticates with supplied credentials/hash material, binds SCM, creates and starts an operator-command service and deletes it. Both SMB dialect execution state machines are implemented.
members.execution_chain: NTLM/SMB session -> SCM RPC create/start/delete service -> command

members.marker_note: MSBuild execution: runs encoded PowerShell through remote MSBuild
members.behavior: The module embeds a CodeTaskFactory C# task hosting a PowerShell runspace, Base64-encodes the command into project XML, writes the project to the target, discovers MSBuild via WMI/registry, and launches it through WMI.
members.execution_chain: Base64 command -> inline-task XML -> target write -> WMI MSBuild launch -> AddScript

members.marker_note: PowerSploit persistence: installs concealed profile and WMI payloads
members.behavior: Add-Persistence generates compressed/encoded code and persistent activation commands for profiles, tasks, registry and WMI subscriptions. Install-SSP additionally installs a supplied security package. Persistence is functional code generated by the module, not only documentation.
members.execution_chain: Add-Persistence -> payload compression -> profile/task/registry/WMI registration; Install-SSP

members.marker_note: Mimikatz test copy: contains a working reflective password dumper
members.behavior: Despite the test directory, the bytes contain an operational reflective loader and complete x86/x64 Mimikatz PEs. Main sets sekurlsa::logonpasswords by default, clears PE magic and invokes the native export. This is not a mock or harmless fixture.
members.execution_chain: Main -> architecture PE decode -> MZ erasure -> reflective native password dispatcher

members.marker_note: Empire native stager: downloads raw code and executes it as a fiber
members.behavior: The C template obtains HTTP(S) bytes into a buffer, allocates executable memory, copies that same buffer, converts the current thread to a fiber, creates a fiber at the downloaded code and switches to it. Host/port/path remain template placeholders.
members.execution_chain: DownloadHostPathToBuffer -> VirtualAlloc RWX -> memcpy -> CreateFiber -> SwitchToFiber

members.marker_note: Empire PowerShell agent: decrypts tasks, executes code and returns files
members.behavior: Routing/session helpers decrypt received task packets. Process-Tasking dispatches commands including IEX of received code, file upload/download chunks and asynchronous jobs; results are encoded/encrypted into response packets. Controller/session configuration must be supplied by staging.
members.execution_chain: task packet decrypt -> Process-Tasking/IEX -> packetized command/file responses

members.marker_note: Empire Python agent: executes received code and transfers local files
members.behavior: The agent dispatches received packet types to compile/exec, shell command, job, file upload/download and discovery handlers. It reads local file chunks, encodes them and returns result packets to its transport.
members.execution_chain: process_packet -> dynamic_code_execute/command/file_download -> send_message

members.marker_note: Empire IronPython agent: executes remote tasks and transfers local files
members.behavior: Along with compile/exec and file transfer handlers, this agent loads supplied managed executables, hosts PowerShell runspaces and offers SOCKS/SMB pipe relay tasks. Packet dispatch connects operator task data to these operations and returned results.
members.execution_chain: process_packet -> Python/PowerShell/.NET handlers -> command/file result packets

members.marker_note: CmdASP webshell: runs posted commands and returns captured output
members.behavior: Request.Form(.CMD) is concatenated into cmd.exe /c and WScript.Shell.Run. Output is redirected to a temporary file, read into the HTTP response and deleted. No application authentication gate is present.
members.execution_chain: Request.Form -> WScript.Shell.Run(cmd /c) -> temp output -> Response.Write -> delete

members.marker_note: PHP backdoor: exposes request-driven commands and file management
members.behavior: The page passes request parameter c directly to system, lets operators read arbitrary files, enumerate directories, upload to a requested directory and run supplied MySQL queries. There is no authentication gate.
members.execution_chain: $_REQUEST -> system/fopen/opendir/move_uploaded_file/mysql_query

members.marker_note: Perl CGI shell: executes the query string and returns its output
members.behavior: The CGI takes QUERY_STRING, decodes space and semicolon sequences, executes the resulting variable with shell backticks, and prints captured lines in the HTTP response.
members.execution_chain: QUERY_STRING -> limited URL decoding -> backtick shell -> response loop

members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP shell: provides authenticated remote shell execution
members.behavior: This injectable shell checks a fixed IP allowlist and configured SHA1 password records, then passes the posted command to proc_open and returns stdout/stderr. Those gates restrict operator access but do not remove its purpose as an injectable shell.
members.execution_chain: IP check -> session authentication -> POST command -> proc_open -> stdout/stderr response

members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP shell: executes HTTP commands behind an IP allowlist
members.behavior: The page checks allowed source IPs, otherwise returns 404. A posted cmd is executed with WScript.Shell.Exec and StdOut/StdErr are sent back. The 404 path is an access-hiding gate, not an absence of command capability.
members.execution_chain: REMOTE_ADDR allowlist -> Request.Form cmd -> WScript.Shell.Exec -> HTTP output

members.marker_note: Laudanum WordPress shell: runs posted commands with auth disabled
members.behavior: The template includes ipcheck.php, but changes the session-authentication gate to if(true) and hides login UI behind if(false). Posted command values reach proc_open; the child output is rendered into the terminal UI. The external IP-check implementation is a dependency, not assumed absent.
members.execution_chain: include ipcheck.php -> unconditional command branch -> POST command -> proc_open -> output

members.marker_note: WordPress plugin shell: executes HTTP commands and locks its own file
members.behavior: The plugin runs chmod to remove write permissions and chattr +i on itself. Request data is passed through executeCommand to reflection/callback/system/passthru variants. An attempted reverse-shell branch uses an undefined $ip key and assumes fd 3, so no reliable working reverse-shell claim is added.
members.execution_chain: $_REQUEST[$cmd] -> executeCommand -> reflected/callback/system execution; chmod/chattr self-lock

members.marker_note: JSP command WAR: executes HTTP parameters and returns process output
members.behavior: The WAR contains a JSP and deployment descriptor. The JSP reads request.getParameter(cmd), passes it directly to Runtime.exec, reads the process input stream and prints returned lines. This is not an inert Java archive.
members.execution_chain: WAR cmd.jsp -> request parameter -> Runtime.exec -> output loop

members.marker_note: Overlapping ZIP bomb: overlaps entries to cause petabyte expansion
members.behavior: Central-directory inspection finds 190023 entries declaring 4507981427706459 uncompressed bytes in a 45876952-byte ZIP. Many compressed ranges overlap. A bounded first-entry read confirms a decoded nested ZIP header; the archive was not fully expanded.
members.execution_chain: ZIP central-directory sizes/ranges -> deliberately overlapping extreme decompression workload

members.marker_note: ZIP traversal depth 1: traversal writes defacement text to index.php
members.behavior: The local header and central directory both name ../index.php. Its complete stored body is hacked followed by newline. This can replace an existing web page outside an unsafe extractor destination; it contains no PHP code, credential theft or shell. Safe extractors reject or sanitize the path.
members.execution_chain: ZIP stored member ../index.php -> hacked\n
